confirmed.title: POST /reports/:id/run mutates persisted state with no permission gate and accepts an arbitrary query override
confirmed.evidence: The route has no preHandler (every other mutating analytics route uses `preHandler: [server.requirePermission('reports:write')]`, e.g. lines 74, 119, 160, 196), yet it creates AnalyticsReportRun rows, bumps report.lastRunAt, and writes an audit log. Worse, line 275: `const query = req.body?.query ?? (report.query as unknown as AnalyticsQuery);` — any authenticated org member WITHOUT reports:write can substitute a completely different query (different entity, filters, aggregates) and have its results persisted into the report's official run history. Dashboards surface that history: analytics-dashboards.ts `latestRunIds()` resolves widget.config.latestRunId to the most recent run, so a read-only user can poison the numbers every dashboard viewer sees for that report (e.g. make a revenue KPI show rows from the `goal`/forecasts entity). Tenant isolation itself holds (compile still injects the caller's org_id), but this is an intra-org privilege/integrity bypass.
confirmed.fix: Add `preHandler: [server.requirePermission('reports:write')]` (or a dedicated reports:run permission) to POST /reports/:id/run; alternatively only persist runs for the stored query and treat body-override runs as ephemeral like POST /reports/run.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.ts:259-293. The POST /reports/:id/run handler has NO preHandler, while every other mutating analytics route gates with `preHandler: [server.requirePermission('reports:write')]` (lines 74, 119, 160, 196). Grep confirms only those 4 preHandlers exist in the file; the run route is not among them, and neither the plugin registration (server.routes.ts:126) nor the auth/rbac plugins apply an instance-wide write gate (rbac.ts only enforces when requirePermission is explicitly attached). The route mutates persisted state: runPersistedReport (analytics-reports.helpers.ts:88-128) creates an AnalyticsReportRun row and bumps report.lastRunAt, and the handler writes an auditLog (lines 281-290). Line 275 (`const query = req.body?.query ?? (report.query ...)`) with body schema `z.object({ query: AnalyticsQuery.optional() }).optional()` lets any authenticated org member without reports:write substitute an arbitrary valid query (different entity/filters/aggregates) and persist it as the report's run. The dashboard amplification is real: analytics-dashboards.ts latestRunIds() (lines 97-109) resolves widget.config.latestRunId to the most recent run per report (orderBy createdAt desc, distinct reportId) and surfaces it to all viewers via serializeWidget, so a read-only user can poison the numbers every dashboard viewer sees. Tenant isolation does hold (analytics-engine.ts:287 always injects `org_id = ${orgId}::uuid` from req.auth.orgId, fields allowlisted), so this is an intra-org broken-access-control / integrity bypass, not a cross-tenant leak. That scope (authenticated same-org, integrity not confidentiality) keeps it at major rather than critical.

confirmed.title: Run result storage is unbounded — no retention, no per-report cap, no rate limit
confirmed.evidence: `runPersistedReport` stores `result: rows as object[]` (up to ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT=1000 full-width rows — a plain row select on `lead` emits ALL 17 allowlisted columns including 500-char BANT text fields) into `analytics_report_runs.result Json` (schema.prisma:4975). Runs are never pruned: GET /reports/:id/runs only `take: 20` (analytics-reports.ts:307) but every POST inserts a new row forever, and there is no rate limit. Combined with the missing permission gate on POST /reports/:id/run, any authenticated user can loop the endpoint and grow the table by multiple MB per request — a storage-exhaustion vector against the shared Postgres instance.
confirmed.fix: On each successful run, delete runs older than the newest N (e.g. 20) per report inside the same transaction; cap serialized result size (reject/truncate above a byte budget); rate-limit the run endpoints.

verdict.reason: Verified at all cited locations. analytics-reports.helpers.ts:108 stores result: rows as object[] into analytics_report_runs.result Json (schema.prisma:4975) on every POST /reports/:id/run. ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT=1000 (analytics-engine.ts:32) and the Zod AnalyticsQuery schema leaves limit uncapped (analytics.ts:131), so clampLimit's 1000 is the only bound. Plain row selects emit ALL allowlisted columns (analytics-engine.ts:279-285); LEAD_FIELDS has exactly 17 fields including 4 BANT string columns recently widened to 500 chars. No retention exists anywhere: only integration tests delete analyticsReportRun rows; the worker prunes yjsUpdate and AI-audit data but not analytics runs; GET /reports/:id/runs take:20 is read-side only. POST /reports/:id/run has no requirePermission preHandler (unlike the reports:write-gated write routes) and no per-route rateLimit config, unlike comparable heavy endpoints. One overstatement: a global per-user rate limit of API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX (default 120/min, server.ts:192-205) does exist, so "no rate limit" is not literally true — but at multiple MB per run, 120 runs/min still permits hundreds of MB/hour of permanent, never-pruned growth, and even legitimate repeated/scheduled runs accumulate unboundedly. Core defect (unbounded storage, no retention, no per-report cap, no permission gate or per-route limit on the run endpoint) is real.

confirmed.title: Raw database error messages persisted to run.error and returned to clients
confirmed.evidence: `const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Query execution failed';` stores the raw exception message on the run row, and `serializeRun` (line 69) ships `error: r.error` on the wire. For non-AnalyticsQueryError failures (e.g. an out-of-range date param like '0000-01-01' which passes Date.parse but fails the ::timestamptz cast), Prisma raw-query errors look like 'Raw query failed. Code: `22008`. Message: ...' and can include generated SQL fragments / table+column names — internal schema disclosure to any org user. Only AnalyticsQueryError messages are written to be client-safe.
confirmed.fix: Persist err.message only when `err instanceof AnalyticsQueryError`; otherwise store a generic 'Query execution failed' and log the real error via the request-scoped Pino logger.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. runPersistedReport (apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.helpers.ts:119-123) persists raw err.message to run.error for ANY Error, with no AnalyticsQueryError discrimination; serializeRun (line 69) ships it, and POST /reports/:id/run plus both GET runs endpoints (analytics-reports.ts:291, :309, :326) return it to any authenticated org user — the AnalyticsReportRun schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:162) passes any string. The trigger is real: coerceScalar's date branch (analytics-engine.ts:79-83) validates only via Date.parse, so '0000-01-01' (valid in JS, no year zero in Postgres) reaches the ::timestamptz cast and fails at execution as a Prisma P2010 error ('Raw query failed. Code: `22008`...'), which is not an AnalyticsQueryError; Zod's value: z.unknown() doesn't block it and the run endpoint skips the dry-compile validateQuery. No downstream guard exists — onSend hooks are header-only and the global error handler is bypassed since the message travels as data in a 200. The preview route (/reports/run line 240-243) rethrows non-AnalyticsQueryError failures instead, confirming only AnalyticsQueryError messages were designed to be client-safe. Minor caveat: the evidence's 'SQL fragments / table+column names' leak is overstated (identifiers are allowlisted; a 22008 message echoes the user's own input), but Prisma/Postgres error codes and messages — and potentially DB host info on connection failures — are disclosed verbatim, so the defect stands as described at minor severity.

confirmed.title: TIME_BUCKET_SQL prototype-key lookup is the one Prisma.raw fed by a non-allowlist string
confirmed.evidence: `const bucket = TIME_BUCKET_SQL[g.timeBucket] ?? fail(...)` followed by `Prisma.raw(`'${bucket}'`)`. TIME_BUCKET_SQL is a plain object, so inherited keys bypass the `?? fail` guard: `timeBucket: 'constructor'` (or 'toString'/'valueOf') returns a truthy Function whose source gets interpolated into raw SQL — e.g. date_trunc('function Object() { [native code] }', ...). Not exploitable today: (a) the Zod enum AnalyticsTimeBucket gates every wire path and both write paths validate stored queries, and (b) V8 function source contains no single quotes so it cannot escape the literal — but this is the only spot where a string not taken verbatim from analytics-fields.ts/a closed switch reaches Prisma.raw, violating the engine's stated standalone invariant ('identifiers come ONLY from analytics-fields.ts').
confirmed.fix: Guard with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(TIME_BUCKET_SQL, g.timeBucket)` (mirroring getEntitySpec) or use a Map — and bind the bucket as a parameter instead of Prisma.raw: `Prisma.sql`date_trunc(${bucket}, ${Prisma.raw(field.column)})`` (date_trunc accepts a text parameter).

verdict.reason: VERIFIED at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:231-232. TIME_BUCKET_SQL (line 38) is a plain object literal (Record<string,string>), not Object.create(null) or a Map, so inherited keys ('constructor'/'toString'/'valueOf') return a truthy Function that bypasses the `?? fail` nullish guard; the resulting `'${bucket}'` would interpolate the function source into Prisma.raw inside date_trunc. The mechanism is real JS behavior and is correctly the ONLY Prisma.raw fed by a non-allowlist dynamic-key lookup: every other Prisma.raw in the file draws from the field allowlist (field.column/spec.table), a literal, or a value already narrowed by a closed switch/equality check (op at 129-130, agg.fn at 205/209, s.dir at 295). This violates the engine's stated standalone invariant. HOWEVER it is a latent defense-in-depth nit, not an active vuln: (a) every wire path gates timeBucket through the Zod enum AnalyticsTimeBucket (schemas/analytics.ts:46, AnalyticsGroupBy.timeBucket :115) — a non-enum value fails Fastify/Zod validation -> 400 before the compiler; write paths dry-compile via validateQuery and the /reports/:id/run stored-query fallback was validated on write; and (b) V8 native function source contains no single quote, so it cannot escape the SQL literal (Postgres would just reject the invalid date_trunc field at runtime). The claim is accurate and honestly self-scoped. Defensible fix: Object.hasOwn / Map / closed switch like the op and agg.fn patterns already used in the same file.

confirmed.title: Unbounded in/notIn arrays and uncapped aggregates/sort lists allow parameter/SQL blowup
confirmed.evidence: `value: z.unknown().optional()` (line 86) puts no bound on `in`/`notIn` arrays; the engine only checks non-empty (analytics-engine.ts:144) and binds every element as a parameter via Prisma.join (line 147-148). The 50-condition budget counts conditions, not array elements, so one condition can carry tens of thousands of bound params (until Fastify's body limit / Postgres's 65535-param protocol cap, which surfaces as 500s). Likewise `aggregates`, `groupBy`, and `sort` arrays (lines 128-131) have no `.max()`, so thousands of COUNT(*) aggregates with distinct aliases or repeated sort terms compile into pathologically large SQL. Pure resource-exhaustion, no injection (everything stays parameterized/allowlisted).
confirmed.fix: Add caps in the Zod schema (e.g. in/notIn ≤ 200 values, aggregates ≤ 20, groupBy ≤ 5, sort ≤ 5) and mirror the checks in the engine for defense-in-depth on stored queries.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at the cited locations. analytics.ts:86 `value: z.unknown().optional()` puts no length bound on `in`/`notIn` arrays; analytics-engine.ts:144 only checks the array is non-empty, and lines 147-148 map every element to a bound parameter via `Prisma.join`, so param count == array length. The condition budget at lines 179-181 increments per condition node (`budget.conditions += 1`), not per array element, so the ANALYTICS_MAX_FILTER_CONDITIONS=50 cap does not constrain a single oversized `in` list. With server.ts:53 bodyLimit at 10 MiB, an authenticated caller (the `/reports/run` preview endpoint at analytics-reports.ts:227 has auth but no `requirePermission` gate) can submit tens of thousands of values in one condition, exceeding Postgres's 65535-parameter protocol cap -> 500s. Likewise `aggregates`/`sort` (analytics.ts:128,131) have no `.max()`: the engine sort loop (lines 292-296) does not dedupe, so a repeated sort term compiles into pathologically large SQL, and distinct explicit aliases let thousands of aggregates through the duplicate-alias guard. It is pure resource exhaustion — everything stays parameterized and allowlisted (no injection). One part of the claim is overstated: `groupBy` cannot actually blow up because `addAlias(g.field)` (line 268) plus the field allowlist bound it to the number of allowlisted fields. Severity 'minor' is appropriate: requires a valid authenticated session, no data exposure or injection, impact limited to a 500 / degraded DB query — a hardening gap (add `.max()` on the value array and on aggregates/sort), not a critical vuln.

confirmed.title: Widget mutations skip the owner-or-admin check that protects the parent dashboard
confirmed.evidence: PATCH/DELETE on the dashboard itself enforce `dashboard.ownerId !== req.auth.userId && !(await isOrgAdmin(req))` → 403 (lines 208-210, 246-248), but POST/PATCH/DELETE /dashboards/:id/widgets/* only require visibility (`findVisibleDashboard`) + reports:write. Any org member with reports:write can therefore add, rewire (point widget.reportId at a different report, line 351), or delete every widget on another user's shared dashboard — defacing content the owner-only rule was written to protect. Intra-org only; reportId is correctly re-verified org-scoped (lines 293-299, 341-347).
confirmed.fix: Apply the same owner-or-admin check to widget create/update/delete on non-owned dashboards, or document that shared dashboards are intentionally collaboratively editable.

verdict.reason: Verified in apps/api/src/routes/analytics-dashboards.ts. Dashboard PATCH/DELETE enforce an explicit owner-or-admin 403 after findVisibleDashboard (lines 207-210, 245-248), but the three widget mutation routes — POST /dashboards/:id/widgets (285-326), PATCH /dashboards/:id/widgets/:widgetId (328-374), DELETE /dashboards/:id/widgets/:widgetId (376-406) — only call findVisibleDashboard plus requirePermission('reports:write'). findVisibleDashboard's owner/admin branch (line 129) applies only when !isShared, so any org member passes for shared dashboards. No compensating guard exists: route registration (server.routes.ts:127) adds nothing, AnalyticsWidgetCreate/Patch Zod schemas (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:241-261) validate shape only, and rbac requirePermission checks the permission key against UserRole/RolePermission, not ownership. Result: any org member with reports:write can add, rewire (reportId update at line 351), or hard-delete (deleteMany at line 390) widgets on another user's shared dashboard, while being forbidden from renaming it — an incoherent asymmetry, not deliberate design. Claim's caveats also check out: intra-org only, and reportId is re-verified org-scoped before write (lines 293-298, 341-346).

confirmed.title: Zero cross-org coverage in the integration tests — tenant isolation only asserted on SQL text
confirmed.evidence: Neither analytics-reports.integration.test.ts nor analytics-dashboards.integration.test.ts creates a second org or asserts a 404/empty result for cross-org access (grep for org2/otherOrg/cross-org returns nothing). The org boundary is verified only as a string match in the unit test (analytics-engine.test.ts:31 `expect(text).toContain('WHERE org_id = $1::uuid ...')`) — no test would fail if a route passed the wrong orgId into compileAnalyticsQuery or dropped orgId from a Prisma where clause (e.g. the runs lookups). For the feature whose whole job is compiling user JSON into raw SQL, the isolation invariant deserves an end-to-end test.
confirmed.fix: Add integration cases: seed org A + org B; org B requests GET/PATCH/DELETE/run on org A's report and dashboard ids (expect 404), and a run on an org-B report over shared tables returns only org-B rows.

verdict.reason: Verified at the cited locations. Both analytics integration suites (apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.integration.test.ts, analytics-dashboards.integration.test.ts) use only the single org_seed_mantu org; grep for org2/otherOrg/cross-org in these files returns nothing. Their 'foreign' tests (reports line 96-105; dashboards line 167-177, despite being labeled 'Cross-tenant reportId rejected') use a nonexistent UUID, which 404s/400s regardless of org scoping — they cannot detect a dropped orgId. The isolation invariant is otherwise asserted only as a SQL-text string match in analytics-engine.test.ts:31 (expect(text).toContain('WHERE org_id = $1::uuid...')) with the org id supplied by the test itself. analytics-reports.ts relies on ~20 Prisma lookups scoped by orgId: req.auth.orgId plus req.auth.orgId passed into compileAnalyticsQuery; removing any of them would break no existing test. Guards elsewhere (Zod schema, field allowlist, auth plugin) constrain query shape and identity but never exercise two tenants in tests. Other suites in the same repo (migrations.*, rfp-pipeline.*, crews) do create a foreign org and assert cross-org 404, so this is a genuine deviation from the codebase's own pattern. Routes are correctly scoped today, so this is a test-coverage gap, not a live leak — minor severity stands.

confirmed.title: Grouped/time-bucketed queries have no deterministic ORDER BY and are silently truncated by LIMIT
confirmed.evidence: `if (orderParts.length === 0 && aggregates.length === 0 && emittedAliases.has('createdAt')) { orderParts.push(Prisma.sql`"createdAt" DESC`); }` — the default ordering applies ONLY to plain row selects. Every aggregate/groupBy query (the line/bar/pie path) gets NO ORDER BY, then `LIMIT ${clampLimit(query.limit)}` (default 100) is appended unconditionally. Postgres GROUP BY (hash agg) output order is unspecified, so: (a) a time-series `groupBy: [{field:'createdAt', timeBucket:'MONTH'}]` returns buckets in arbitrary order — charts plot scrambled series; (b) a groupBy on a high-cardinality field (e.g. lead `companyName`) with >100 groups silently drops an ARBITRARY subset of groups, so totals are wrong with no error. No test covers ordering or truncation of grouped output.
confirmed.fix: When groupBy is present and no sort is given, default to ORDER BY the groupBy expressions (ASC for timeBucket). Consider rejecting or flagging grouped queries whose group count hits the LIMIT.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:297-305. The default ORDER BY ("createdAt" DESC) is gated on aggregates.length === 0, and lines 252-255 inject a synthetic COUNT(*) aggregate for any groupBy-without-aggregates query, so EVERY grouped/aggregate query (all chart paths) compiles with no ORDER BY unless the client explicitly sends sort. LIMIT (default 100 via clampLimit) is appended unconditionally at line 305. No guard exists elsewhere: the Zod schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:130) makes sort optional with no refinement tying it to groupBy, and executeAnalyticsQuery (apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.helpers.ts:79) passes the query straight to the compiler with no default sort injection. Postgres hash-aggregate output order is unspecified, so (a) unsorted time-bucket series return buckets in arbitrary order and (b) groupBy on a >100-cardinality field silently returns an arbitrary subset of groups with no error. Test coverage confirms the gap: analytics-engine.test.ts asserts the default ORDER BY only for plain row selects (line 179) and tests explicit sort on grouped queries, but no test covers default ordering or LIMIT truncation of grouped output. Partial mitigation only: clients CAN pass sort (group-field and aggregate aliases are sortable), but nothing requires or defaults it.

confirmed.title: Run endpoints skip reports:write and persist runs for arbitrary query overrides, poisoning run history
confirmed.evidence: POST `/reports/:id/run` has no `preHandler: [server.requirePermission('reports:write')]` (unlike create/patch/delete/duplicate) yet it WRITES: creates an AnalyticsReportRun row, stores up to 1000 result rows in `result`, and bumps `report.lastRunAt` (helpers.ts:101-115). It also accepts `body.query` as a full override (`const query = req.body?.query ?? (report.query as ...)`, line 275) — the override run is persisted against the report with NO record of which query produced it (AnalyticsReportRun has no query column, schema.prisma:4967-4984). GET `/reports/:id/runs` then returns rows whose `result`/`rowCount` do not correspond to `report.query`, and the dashboard widget `latestRunId` (analytics-dashboards.ts:96-109) will happily point a KPI widget at an override run's data. Any authenticated org user without reports:write can do all of this.
confirmed.fix: Either require reports:write on the persisted-run route, or persist the effective query on the run row; at minimum mark override runs (e.g. `isAdHoc`) and exclude them from latestRunId/lastRunAt.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.ts:259-293. POST /reports/:id/run has no preHandler while create/patch/duplicate/delete all require reports:write (lines 74/119/160/196); RBAC plugin (plugins/rbac.ts) is opt-in per route and the global auth hook only authenticates, so any authenticated org user (or read-scope API key) can invoke it. The handler accepts a full query override (line 275: `req.body?.query ?? report.query`) and runPersistedReport (analytics-reports.helpers.ts:88-128) persists an AnalyticsReportRun with up to 1000 result rows (ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT clamp, analytics-engine.ts:31-32,305) and bumps report.lastRunAt. AnalyticsReportRun has no query column (schema.prisma:4967-4984) and the audit log diff records only {runId, status}, so override runs are indistinguishable from real runs. GET /reports/:id/runs returns them, and analytics-dashboards.ts:96-109 latestRunIds wires the newest run (override or not) into widget config.latestRunId, so shared dashboards display poisoned data. Mitigating guards exist (Zod AnalyticsQuery schema, engine field allowlist, org-scoped SQL) but they only prevent injection/cross-org reads, not the missing write authorization or run-history poisoning. The sibling POST /reports/run preview endpoint is explicitly ephemeral, confirming persisted override runs are unintended.

confirmed.title: Empty OR filter group compiles to TRUE — wrong identity element widens results
confirmed.evidence: `if (parts.length === 0) return Prisma.sql`TRUE`;` regardless of `group.logic`. TRUE is the identity for AND, but the identity for OR is FALSE. A nested `{logic:'OR', conditions:[]}` inside an AND tree (exactly what a filter-builder UI emits when the user adds a group before any condition) becomes a no-op TRUE instead of matching nothing or erroring, so the preview silently returns ALL rows as if the group passed. The wire schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:98-104) allows `conditions: []`, so this is reachable.
confirmed.fix: Reject empty groups with AnalyticsQueryError (preferred), or return FALSE for empty OR groups.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:186 — buildFilterGroup returns Prisma.sql`TRUE` for any empty group before consulting group.logic, so an empty OR group becomes a no-op (TRUE) instead of the correct OR identity (FALSE) or an error. Reachable: the Zod schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:98-104) allows conditions: [] with no .min(1), and the call chain (analytics-reports.ts:37, analytics-reports.helpers.ts:79 -> compileAnalyticsQuery line 289) has no pruning or empty-group guard. Not intentional leniency: the engine hard-fails the analogous empty-disjunction case (`in` with empty array, lines 144-146) with a test locking that strictness in (analytics-engine.test.ts:201-218), while line 186 has no comment and no test. Org scoping (line 287) is applied outside the filter tree, so impact is over-broad results within the tenant only — severity minor is correct.

confirmed.title: Number coercion accepts '' / arrays / 'Infinity' — compiles wrong predicates instead of 400
confirmed.evidence: `const n = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value); if (typeof value === 'boolean' || value == null || Number.isNaN(n)) fail(...)` — `Number('')` === 0, `Number('  ')` === 0, `Number([])` === 0, `Number([5])` === 5, `Number('Infinity')` === Infinity; none are NaN, so a filter `{field:'score', operator:'eq', value:''}` (empty input box) compiles to `score = 0` and returns real rows instead of a 400. The value is `z.unknown()` on the wire (analytics.ts:86) so all of these reach the engine.
confirmed.fix: Only accept `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value)` or a string matching a strict numeric regex; reject everything else.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:71-77. coerceScalar's number branch computes Number(value) and rejects only booleans, null/undefined, and NaN — but Number('')===0, Number('  ')===0, Number([])===0, Number([5])===5, Number('Infinity')===Infinity, none NaN, so all pass. The wire schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:86) types filter value as z.unknown().optional(), and the route (analytics-reports.ts:231-241) validates only shape before calling compileAnalyticsQuery, so these values reach the engine unfiltered. buildCondition passes cond.value directly to coerceScalar for eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte with no array check (the array guard only covers in/notIn), so {field:'score', operator:'eq', value:''} compiles to a bound `score = 0` predicate and returns real rows instead of a 400; 'Infinity' compiles to an Infinity parameter that errors at the DB (500) on integer/numeric columns. Field allowlist checks names only; numeric fields (score, valueMicros, amountMicros, etc.) exist. No injection or tenancy impact (values are parameterized, org_id scoping intact), and no test pins the current behavior — it is a validation gap producing silently wrong results, matching the claimed minor severity.

confirmed.title: JS Date.parse accepts strings Postgres rejects — preview route 500s instead of 400
confirmed.evidence: `if (typeof value !== 'string' || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(value))) fail(...); return Prisma.sql`${value}::timestamptz`;` — validation runs in JS but parsing runs in Postgres on the ORIGINAL string. Node's `Date.parse('0')` is valid (year 2000), but `'0'::timestamptz` raises 22007 in Postgres, which surfaces as a raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError. In POST /reports/run (analytics-reports.ts:240-242) only AnalyticsQueryError maps to 400, so this returns HTTP 500; in runPersistedReport it lands as a cryptic driver message in run.error. The two parsers disagree on a whole family of inputs ('1', '0', bare numbers, some locale formats).
confirmed.fix: Validate with a strict ISO-8601 regex (date or full timestamp) instead of Date.parse, or normalize to `new Date(value).toISOString()` before binding.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:78-84: the date branch gates on JS Date.parse but binds the original string with a ::timestamptz cast, and the two parsers genuinely disagree. Verified empirically that Node's Date.parse('0') returns 946702800000 (year 2000, not NaN), while Postgres rejects '0'::timestamptz with SQLSTATE 22007. No upstream guard exists: AnalyticsFilterCondition.value is z.unknown() in packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:86, and the field allowlist exposes many date fields (createdAt, dueDate, etc.), so {field:'createdAt', operator:'gt', value:'0'} reaches the engine. In POST /reports/run (apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.ts:238-243) only AnalyticsQueryError maps to 400; the resulting Prisma raw-query failure is P2010, which the global error handler (apps/api/src/plugins/error-handler.ts) does not map (only P2002/P2025/P2003), so it falls through to a generic 500. In runPersistedReport (analytics-reports.helpers.ts:116-123) the raw driver message is persisted to run.error as claimed. Minor inaccuracy in the claim: the 500 body is the sanitized generic 'Something went wrong', not a raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError serialization — the status-code defect stands regardless.

confirmed.title: Micros money aggregates cast to ::float8 — silent integer precision loss past 2^53 micros
confirmed.evidence: `return Prisma.sql`${Prisma.raw(agg.fn)}(${col})::float8`;` for SUM/AVG (and MIN/MAX numeric). `value_micros`/`amount_micros` are BigInt columns (schema.prisma:378, 2755) per the repo money rule ("store amounts in micros (integer)"). SUM(value_micros) in Postgres is exact NUMERIC, but the ::float8 cast rounds once the aggregate exceeds 2^53 ≈ 9.007e15 micros (≈ €9.0B) — an org-wide multi-year pipeline sum silently loses low-order digits. Same hazard in normalizeAnalyticsRows (line 320): `if (typeof value === 'bigint') out[key] = Number(value)`. Nothing in the wire contract marks these as inexact.
confirmed.fix: Return money aggregates as strings (drop ::float8, serialize Decimal/BigInt via .toString()) or document/clamp the float8 contract explicitly; format at the edge per repo convention.

verdict.reason: Verified at the cited location. analytics-engine.ts lines 202-211 cast SUM/AVG (and numeric MIN/MAX) to ::float8, and line 320 converts bigint driver values via Number(). The aggregated columns are BigInt micros (schema.prisma: Opportunity.valueMicros @map("value_micros"), Forecast.amountMicros @map("amount_micros")) and both are allowlisted as type 'number' in analytics-fields.ts (lines 88, 207), so SUM(value_micros)::float8 is reachable. Postgres SUM(bigint) is exact NUMERIC; the float8 cast silently rounds once the aggregate exceeds 2^53 micros (~€9.0B). No guard exists: the Zod schema in packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts validates query shape only (no mention of precision/safe-integer), and executeAnalyticsQuery in analytics-reports.helpers.ts pipes raw rows straight through normalizeAnalyticsRows into a Json column / JSON wire format with nothing marking the values inexact. The defect exists exactly as described, violating the repo money rule (store micros as exact integers). Severity 'minor' is appropriate: the threshold (~€9B org-wide sum) is a far edge case for this product, and below 2^53 the float8 integers are exact.

confirmed.title: No statement timeout or execution-cost cap on the user-shaped raw query
confirmed.evidence: `const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<...>(sql)` runs the compiled query with no `statement_timeout` and no Fastify request timeout. The LIMIT clamp (analytics-engine.ts:305) bounds output rows, not work: GROUP BY aggregates scan entire tenant tables, and the filter grammar permits up to 50 OR'd `ILIKE '%...%'` conditions (analytics-engine.ts:132-141, cap at line 34/180) which defeat indexes and force seq scans on large tables (activities). One slow query holds a Prisma pool connection until Postgres finishes; a handful of concurrent runs can exhaust the pool and stall the whole API.
confirmed.fix: Execute inside prisma.$transaction with `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '10s'` (or an equivalent pool/server-level timeout) so runaway queries are cancelled, and surface the cancellation as run.status='error'.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.helpers.ts:79-81 — prisma.$queryRaw(sql) executes the user-shaped query with no timeout or cancellation at any layer. Repo-wide grep finds zero statement_timeout settings; PrismaClient (packages/db/src/index.ts:19-21) is constructed with only a log option (no datasource URL options, no connection_limit/pool_timeout); the Fastify constructor (apps/api/src/server.ts:52) sets no requestTimeout/connectionTimeout (Fastify defaults: disabled), and an HTTP timeout could not cancel the Postgres query anyway. The queryGuardPlugin only logs slow queries post-hoc. Evidence details all check out: the LIMIT clamp (analytics-engine.ts:305, max 1000) bounds output rows after GROUP BY aggregation work; contains/startsWith compile to ILIKE with leading % (analytics-engine.ts:132-141) which defeats indexes; up to 50 OR'd conditions allowed (cap at lines 34/180-181) and the shared Zod schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:98-104) adds no tighter bound; the entity allowlist includes activities (analytics-fields.ts:219). The preview endpoint POST /reports/run (analytics-reports.ts:227-255) lets any authenticated user run arbitrary schema-valid queries synchronously; the per-user per-minute rate limit does not bound concurrent in-flight queries, so a handful of slow queries can exhaust Prisma's default pool (num_cpus*2+1) and stall all DB-backed endpoints (P2024 pool timeouts). Tempering factors — auth required, queries are single-table and org-scoped with no JOINs (worst case O(tenant rows x 50 ILIKE patterns)) — bound the blast radius but do not refute the defect.

confirmed.title: run.error persists raw Prisma/driver error text and returns it to clients with HTTP 200, bypassing the sanitizing error handler; failures are never logged
confirmed.evidence: `const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Query execution failed'` stores err.message verbatim in the run row, and serializeRun (line 69) ships it to the client. Prisma raw-query failures read like "Raw query failed. Code: `42...`. Message: `<db error>`" and PrismaClientInitializationError messages include the DB host/port ("Can't reach database server at `host:5432`"). The centralized handler deliberately hides exactly this class of detail for 5xx (apps/api/src/plugins/error-handler.ts:56-74: "may contain DB connection strings ... ORM internals"), but the run.error path returns it inside a 200 response. The catch also swallows the error without any Pino logging — engine/DB failures are invisible to ops.
confirmed.fix: Persist err.message only when `err instanceof AnalyticsQueryError`; otherwise store a generic 'Query execution failed' and log the real error with the request-scoped logger (pass it into runPersistedReport).

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.helpers.ts:119-123: the catch persists err.message verbatim to run.error with no Pino logging, serializeRun (line 69) forwards it, and POST /reports/:id/run (analytics-reports.ts:259-292, schema response {200: AnalyticsReportRun}) returns it in an HTTP 200; AnalyticsReportRun.error is z.string().optional() (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:162) so Zod passes raw text through. This bypasses the centralized handler (plugins/error-handler.ts:56-74) which deliberately hides 5xx detail AND does the only error logging — so engine/DB failures are never logged (the audit-log write records only runId+status). Non-AnalyticsQueryError failures reaching this catch are raw Prisma errors: user-triggerable via the Date.parse-vs-Postgres laxness in coerceScalar (analytics-engine.ts:78-83, `${value}::timestamptz` → 'Raw query failed. Code: 22007...'), plus statement timeouts and mid-request connection loss; raw text is also re-served by GET /reports/:id/runs[/:runId]. One evidence overstatement: the PrismaClientInitializationError host:port leak largely self-limits because the pre-try run.create or the in-catch updateMany would also fail and bubble to the sanitized 500 handler; realistic leaks are PG error codes/messages and ORM internals to authenticated same-org users. Core claim stands: raw driver text persisted + returned in 200, sanitizer bypassed, failures invisible to ops.

confirmed.title: GET /reports/:id/runs returns full result blobs for 20 runs (multi-MB responses, all loaded in memory)
confirmed.evidence: `prisma.analyticsReportRun.findMany({ where: {...}, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take: 20 })` has no `select`, and `runs.map(serializeRun)` includes `result` (helpers.ts:68). Each persisted result holds up to ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT=1000 normalized rows (lead rows include 500-char BANT text fields), so the history listing can materialize and return ~20 full result sets — tens of MB per request — for what the UI needs as a status list.
confirmed.fix: In the list endpoint, `select` only metadata columns (id, status, startedAt, finishedAt, rowCount, error, createdAt) and omit `result`; serve the payload only from GET /reports/:id/runs/:runId.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.ts:304-309: GET /reports/:id/runs runs analyticsReportRun.findMany with take: 20 and no select, so the full `result` JSON blob of each run is loaded into memory; serializeRun (apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.helpers.ts:68) copies `result` into the response, and the Zod response schema AnalyticsReportRun (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:161) explicitly includes `result: z.array(z.record(z.unknown())).optional()`, so the fastify-type-provider-zod serializer ships all 20 blobs to the client — no guard strips them. Blob size is realistic: runPersistedReport persists the full row set (helpers.ts:108), ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT=1000 (analytics-engine.ts:32) is reachable via saved query limit (AnalyticsQuery.limit has no Zod max), and non-aggregate queries select every allowlisted column including the four 500-char lead BANT text columns (analytics-engine.ts:279-285, analytics-fields.ts:57-60). A dedicated GET /reports/:id/runs/:runId endpoint already exists for fetching a single run's result, confirming the history listing doesn't need the blobs. Caveat: ANALYTICS_DEFAULT_LIMIT=100 and aggregate results are small, so worst case needs raw-row reports with high explicit limits — but the structural defect (N full result sets fetched and returned for a status list, no pagination/projection) exists exactly as described.

confirmed.title: Unbounded run-result storage: every run persists up to 1000 rows of Json and runs are never pruned
confirmed.evidence: `result: rows as object[]` stores the full (clamped-to-1000-row) result set on every POST /reports/:id/run. Reads only `take: 20` (analytics-reports.ts:307) but nothing ever deletes older rows — AnalyticsReportRun (schema.prisma:4967-4980) has no retention mechanism and no code path prunes it. Dashboard auto-refresh or repeated manual runs grow analytics_report_runs (and its Json payloads) without bound; this also feeds the in-memory distinct defect in latestRunIds.
confirmed.fix: After a successful run, delete runs beyond the newest N (e.g. 20, matching the read cap) per report inside the same transaction; optionally store `result` only on the latest run or cap its serialized size.

verdict.reason: Verified at the cited locations. analytics-reports.helpers.ts:94 creates a new analyticsReportRun row on every POST /reports/:id/run, and lines 101-110 persist the full result set (`result: rows as object[]`). The only size bound is the engine clamp (analytics-engine.ts:31-32, 239-241, 305: ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT=1000, default 100); the Zod AnalyticsQuery schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:131) leaves `limit` uncapped, so no upstream guard reduces the stored payload. Reads use take:20 (analytics-reports.ts:307), yet a repo-wide search finds zero pruning: the only analyticsReportRun.deleteMany calls are in two integration test files, and the worker app — which has retention jobs for other tables (rfp.audit-cleanup 90d, yjs-compaction 30d) — has none for analytics_report_runs. schema.prisma:4967-4984 confirms `result Json?` with no TTL; the only deletion path is FK cascade on report/org hard delete, but report deletion in the API is soft (deletedAt, analytics-reports.ts:205-209), so runs of deleted reports persist forever, slightly strengthening the claim. The run endpoint also has no requirePermission gate or rate limit, so repeated manual runs or dashboard auto-refresh grow the table without bound. Defect exists exactly as described.

confirmed.title: latestRunIds uses Prisma in-memory `distinct` — fetches every run row for the referenced reports on each dashboard read
confirmed.evidence: `prisma.analyticsReportRun.findMany({ where: { orgId, reportId: { in: reportIds } }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, distinct: ['reportId'], ... })` — on Prisma 5.22 without the `nativeDistinct` preview flag (packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma generator: previewFeatures = ["postgresqlExtensions"] only), `distinct` is applied in the query engine AFTER fetching all matching rows; it does not emit SQL DISTINCT ON. So GET /api/v1/dashboards (which hydrates ALL widgets across all visible dashboards, line 150-151) pulls every run ever created for those reports into memory on every read. Combined with the missing run pruning, dashboard latency and API memory degrade linearly and unboundedly with run count. The comment on line 100-101 claiming 'no N+1' masks this.
confirmed.fix: Replace with a raw `SELECT DISTINCT ON (report_id) id, report_id FROM analytics_report_runs WHERE org_id = $1 AND report_id = ANY($2) ORDER BY report_id, created_at DESC`, or enable the nativeDistinct preview feature.

verdict.reason: Verified at apps/api/src/routes/analytics-dashboards.ts:102-107: findMany uses distinct:['reportId'] + orderBy createdAt desc with no take. packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:7 enables only ["postgresqlExtensions"] (Prisma ^5.22.0), so nativeDistinct is off and Prisma applies distinct in-memory in the query engine after fetching ALL rows matching the where clause — no SQL DISTINCT ON or LIMIT is emitted. GET /dashboards (lines 140-152) calls latestRunIds over all widgets of all visible dashboards on every read; the same helper backs GET /dashboards/:id and /:id/widgets. Run rows grow unboundedly: every report execution creates one (analytics-reports.helpers.ts:94 via analytics-reports.ts:276) and the only deleteMany calls are in integration tests — no pruning exists. No guard in Zod schemas, field allowlists, or auth changes this. Mitigant: select is only {id, reportId} (two UUIDs/row), excluding the large result Json, so the per-row constant is small — but transfer and engine memory still scale linearly and unboundedly with total run count on the hottest analytics read path. The 'no N+1' comment is accurate on query count but masks row volume.

confirmed.title: onDelete: SetNull is dead code — report deletion is soft, leaving widgets with dangling reportId references
confirmed.evidence: `report AnalyticsReport? @relation(fields: [reportId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)` only fires on a hard DELETE, but DELETE /api/v1/reports/:id soft-deletes (`data: { deletedAt: new Date() }`, analytics-reports.ts:205-220) and never touches widgets. After deletion, widget.reportId still points at a report whose GET 404s (deletedAt:null filter, analytics-reports.ts:108-111), while latestRunIds (analytics-dashboards.ts:89,102-108) still injects a latestRunId for the deleted report's runs into widget.config — the dashboard serves widgets bound to an unreachable report. serializeWidget handles reportId=null correctly (line 66), but the soft-delete path can never produce null, so that handling never engages.
confirmed.fix: In the report-delete transaction, add `prisma.analyticsDashboardWidget.updateMany({ where: { reportId: existing.id, orgId }, data: { reportId: null } })` (mirroring the SetNull intent), or filter widget.reportId against live reports during dashboard hydration.

verdict.reason: Verified at all cited locations. schema.prisma:5021 has onDelete: SetNull on AnalyticsDashboardWidget.report, but DELETE /reports/:id (analytics-reports.ts:205-220) only sets deletedAt in a transaction with an audit-log insert — no widget cleanup, and a repo-wide grep shows no production code ever hard-deletes AnalyticsReport (only integration-test cleanup), so SetNull never fires in app flows. After soft-delete, GET /reports/:id 404s (deletedAt:null filter, lines 108-111), yet latestRunIds (analytics-dashboards.ts:97-108) queries runs by reportId with no deletedAt check on the parent report, so all dashboard/widget GET routes still serialize the stale reportId and inject latestRunId into widget.config. serializeWidget's null handling (line 66) can never engage. Guards checked: widget create/patch validate reportId against non-deleted reports at write time only (analytics-dashboards.ts:293-298, 341-346); Zod schemas validate shape only; no cleanup job. Additional nuance: GET /reports/:id/runs/:runId (analytics-reports.ts:313-328) skips the report deletedAt check, so the injected run remains fetchable — widgets can serve data from a deleted report while the report resource 404s. Defect exists exactly as described.

confirmed.title: No concurrent-run dedup and no permission gate on the run/preview endpoints
confirmed.evidence: POST /reports/:id/run (line 259-267) and POST /reports/run (line 227-234) are the only non-GET routes without `preHandler: [server.requirePermission(...)]`, and nothing dedups concurrent runs of the same report — N parallel requests start N parallel raw queries and persist N 1000-row result blobs plus N audit rows. Combined with the missing statement timeout, any authenticated org member can tie up the Prisma connection pool by hammering an expensive report.
confirmed.fix: If a run for the report is already 'running', return that run instead of creating a new one (findFirst status:'running' before create, or a partial unique index), and add an appropriate requirePermission to both execution endpoints.

verdict.reason: Verified in apps/api/src/routes/analytics-reports.ts: POST /reports/run (lines 227-234) and POST /reports/:id/run (lines 259-267) are the only non-GET routes in the file without preHandler: [server.requirePermission('reports:write')] — POST /reports (74), PATCH (119), duplicate (160), and DELETE (196) all have it. RBAC (plugins/rbac.ts) is per-route opt-in and the global auth hook (plugins/auth.ts:368) only authenticates, so any authenticated org member can run reports; line 264 even allows a body query override, letting a non-privileged member execute arbitrary allowlisted queries. No dedup exists: runPersistedReport (analytics-reports.helpers.ts:88-128) unconditionally creates a 'running' row and executes prisma.$queryRaw with no in-flight check, lock, or idempotency key, so N parallel requests produce N raw queries, N persisted result blobs (up to 1000 rows each per ANALYTICS_MAX_LIMIT) and N auditLog rows (route line 281). No statement timeout is set in the engine. Partial mitigation found: a global per-user rate limit of 120 req/min in production (server.ts:192-205, env.ts:87) caps the hammering vector, and queries are Zod-validated, field-allowlisted, org-scoped, and row-capped at 1000 — these bound the impact and justify keeping severity at minor rather than escalating.

confirmed.title: Number coercion silently maps garbage filter values to 0 instead of rejecting them
confirmed.evidence: `const n = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value)` with only boolean/null/NaN rejected: `Number('')` → 0, `Number('  ')` → 0, `Number([])` → 0, `Number(['5'])` → 5. A widget filter with an empty/array value (value is z.unknown() on the wire, schemas/analytics.ts:86) silently compiles to `col = 0` and returns wrong data instead of failing fast with 400 — a malformed saved report degrades into quietly incorrect charts rather than a visible error.
confirmed.fix: Accept only `typeof value === 'number'` or a non-empty numeric string (`typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() !== '' && !Number.isNaN(Number(value))`); fail everything else.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at apps/api/src/lib/analytics-engine.ts:71-77. The guard only rejects boolean, null/undefined, and NaN — but Number('') === 0, Number('  ') === 0, Number([]) === 0, and Number(['5']) === 5, none of which are NaN, so they pass and silently compile to `col = 0` (or 5). No upstream guard exists: the wire schema (packages/shared/src/schemas/analytics.ts:86) types filter value as z.unknown().optional(), the field allowlist validates only field keys, and routes (analytics-reports.ts:37, analytics-reports.helpers.ts:79) pass the parsed query straight to compileAnalyticsQuery. The engine's own pattern is fail-fast (it rejects garbage dates, non-boolean booleans, out-of-set enums, and NaN strings), and analytics-engine.test.ts has no number-coercion tests, so this is an inconsistency/oversight, not intentional. Result: a malformed saved report degrades into quietly wrong query results instead of a 400.
